title: FERC Compliance Directives — Docket P-2067-062: Letter to South San Joaquin Irrigation and Oakdale Irrigation District acknowledging the 06/03/2026 et al. of plan and schedule to satisfy Article 405 of license requirements, etc. for the Tulloch Hydroelectric Project under P-2067.
text:
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
Washington, D. C. 20426
OFFICE OF ENERGY PROJECTS
Project No. 2067-062 – California
Tulloch Hydroelectric Project
South San Joaquin Irrigation and
Oakdale Irrigation District
September 1, 2026
VIA Electronic Mail
Ms. Summer Nicotero
General Manager
Tri-Dam Project
snicotero@tridamproject.com
Subject: Acknowledgement of Plan and Schedule to Satisfy License Requirements,
Pursuant to Article 405, Comments Received Related to Aquatic Nuisance
Weed Management, and Notification of Violation of License Article 405.
Dear Ms. Nicotero:
This letter acknowledges multiple filings regarding vegetation management and
aquatic nuisance vegetation management, including your April 3, 2026 and June 3, 2026
filings in response to the Commission’s February 3, 2026 letter (Commission letter)
notifying you of violations of license Article 405 for the Tulloch Hydroelectric Project
No. 2067.1
Additionally, this letter discusses comments and allegations concerning your
implementation of the approved Vegetation Management Plan (VMP)2 and the approved
Aquatic Nuisance Vegetation Management Plan (ANVMP).3 As discussed in more detail
1 South San Joaquin and Oakdale Irrigation Districts, 114 FERC ¶ 62,162 (2006).
2 South San Joaquin and Oakdale Irrigation Districts, 124 FERC ¶ 62,006 (2008).
3 South San Joaquin and Oakdale Irrigation Districts, 154 FERC ¶ 62,196 (2016).

Project No. 2067-062 - 2 -
below, we find you remain in violation of your project license and provide further
direction.
Background
By letter dated February 3, 2026, Commission staff found that implementation of
the approved ANVMP has not achieved the ANVMP goals and objectives and does not
fulfill the requirements of Article 405. Additionally, the approved ANVMP does not
include (1) provisions for training project staff; (2) provisions for advising resource
agencies of aquatic nuisance vegetation populations on lands these agencies manage
within the project boundary and coordinating with these agencies regarding eradication or
control efforts; and (3) provisions for the identification, mapping, management, and
monitoring of wetlands and important habitat, pursuant to Article 405. Commission staff
required you to make the changes necessary to satisfy the requirements of Article 405
with the ANVMP and review the ANVMP in consultation with the required resource
agencies, allowing sufficient time for stakeholder consultation. You are then required to
file any proposed amendments with the Commission for review and approval.
Commission staff also found that you are in violation of Article 405 of the project
license on the basis that: (1) you have failed to file VMP reports as specified by the
Order Modifying and Approving Vegetation Management Plan Pursuant to Article 405
(2008 Order); (2) you did not complete the aquatic nuisance vegetation monitoring,
aquatic nuisance vegetation control, project staff training, or public outreach and
education measures as required by the license article; and (3) you have documented an
increase in aquatic nuisance vegetation (which has led to the degradation of the lake for
homeowners and recreational users) without implementing management actions to
achieve the objectives of the ANVMP approved by the Order Modifying and Approving
Aquatic Nuisance Vegetation Management Plan (2016 Order). In our letter, we
specifically asked you to: 1) file the missing VMP reports as required by the 2008 Order
within 60 days; and 2) file a plan and schedule to implement the requirements of Article
405 of the project license for Commission approval within 120 days of receipt of the
Commission letter. The Commission’s letter included an attached Schedule A that
outlined the requirements of Article 405 and the 2008 and 2016 Orders. You were
required to develop the plan and schedule in consultation with the U.S. Bureau of
Reclamation (BOR), U.S. Bureau of Land Management (BLM), California Department of
Fish and Game (California DFW), Calaveras County, and Tuolumne County, allowing a
minimum of 30 days for the consulted entities to commend and to make
recommendations before filing the plan with the Commission. You were required to
include documentation of consultation with the specified entities, copies of comments,
and recommendations made in connection with the plan, and a description of how the

Project No. 2067-062 - 3 -
plan accommodates the comments and recommendations. If you did not adopt a
recommendation, the filing was to include your reasons, based on project-specific
information.
Vegetation Management Plan Reports
On April 3, 2026, you filed a response to the Commission’s request to file the
missing VMP reports. You stated that you conducted a comprehensive records review,
including evaluation of electronic and hard-copy project files which identified evidence
of vegetation-related activities, including site observations, coordination efforts, and
implementation measures [unspecified] conducted over time. However, you were unable
to locate any documentation of terrestrial noxious weed monitoring surveys or control
actions. You provided a list of actions you implemented or intended to implement to
satisfy the requirements of Article 405 and the 2008 and 2016 Orders, including but not
limited to: (1) planning and conducting a comprehensive terrestrial noxious weed and
aquatic nuisance vegetation survey within the project boundary, consistent with the
requirements of Article 405, during the 2026 growing season; (2) manually removing
(hand-pulling) terrestrial noxious weeds, including root systems where feasible, ensuring
proper disposal of all materials to prevent re-establishment or spread; (3) investigating
the feasibility of GIS-based mapping to identify the species, location, and extent of
coverage of terrestrial noxious weeds and aquatic nuisance vegetation;4 (4) initiating
and/or continuing consultation with the required resource agencies, California Division of
Boating and Waterways (California DBW),5 the University of California Cooperative
Extension (UCCE),6 and a qualified consultant to support the development of survey
methodology, species identification, and vegetation management efforts, allowing
consulting parties a minimum of 30 days to review and comment on all survey results and
reports; (5) filing the 2026 terrestrial noxious weed survey and aquatic nuisance
vegetation survey reports with the Commission by December 31, 2026, including survey
methodology, mapping, and documentation of agency consultation and comments; (6)
implementing annual terrestrial noxious weed and aquatic nuisance vegetation
monitoring and control measures consistent with the requirements of license Article 405,
beginning in 2026. You also indicated you would provide further details regarding the
4 Commission staff notes that you are required to include documentation of the
areal extent, density of growth, and GIS data for each individual population of terrestrial
noxious weeds and aquatic nuisance vegetation in both the VMP and ANVMP reports.
5 Commission staff notes that your filing referred to the California Department of
Boating and Waterways.
6 Commission staff notes that you included documentation of consultation with
UCCE your April 3, 2026 filing. You did not include documentation of consultation with
California DBW or the required resource agencies.

Project No. 2067-062 - 4 -
terrestrial noxious weed and aquatic nuisance vegetation management and control plan
implementation schedule and program components as well as documentation of
consultation with the upcoming compliance plan and schedule filing.
Process Plan and Schedule
On June 3, 2026, you filed a plan and schedule (Process Plan) to satisfy the
requirements of Article 405, including documentation of consultation, copies of
comments, and your responses to those comments. The Process Plan outlines the actions
you have already implemented to satisfy the requirements of Article 405, including: (1)
on May 11, 2026 you conducted a terrestrial noxious weed survey throughout shoreline
areas within the project boundary, which you state establishes a baseline for future
monitoring and comparison of terrestrial noxious weed populations; (2) manually
removing (hand-pulling) of terrestrial noxious weeds, including removal of root systems
where feasible, with appropriate collection and disposal to prevent re-establishment or
spread; (3) you consulted with the required resource agencies, California Department of
Boating and Waterways, and the University of California Cooperative Extension to
support the development of survey methodology, species identification materials, and
control methods; (4) you performed public outreach efforts, including: (a) distributing an
electronic vegetation management information update to shoreline property owners and
homeowners associations on May 28, 2026 via email; (b) maintaining a dedicated
Vegetation Management webpage that provides educational materials regarding aquatic
nuisance vegetation and terrestrial noxious weeds;7 (c) updating public informational
kiosks throughout the project area with your 2026 Vegetation Management Brochure,
which contains information on aquatic nuisance vegetation;8 and (d) developing a “How-
To” Guidance Sheet for shoreline property owners for distribution via quarterly
newsletters, brochures provided at community events [unspecified], and the Tri-Dam
website, beginning by June 30, 2026.9
7 You propose to include species identification information, approved vegetation
management methods, permitting requirements, prevention measures, an educational
brochure, application forms, the location of known problem areas, and guidance
regarding practices to prevent the spread of invasive vegetation on your Vegetation
Management webpage.
8 You propose to include information regarding aquatic nuisance vegetation
identification, approved management methods, prevention practices, the location of
known problem areas, and a QR code linking directly to Tri-Dam’s vegetation
management webpage in the brochure.
9 You propose to include information on the identification of common aquatic
nuisance vegetation (with a visual guide), the location of known problem areas, best

Project No. 2067-062 - 5 -
The Process Plan proposes additional actions to satisfy the requirements of Article
405, including but not limited to: (1) conducting terrestrial noxious weed and aquatic
nuisance vegetation training (training) beginning in 2026 using aquatic nuisance
vegetation management training materials updated by Tri-Dam staff; (2) retaining a
qualified biologist to evaluate and update the training materials and conduct biennial
training beginning in 2027, with Tri-Dam staff conducting refresher training in non-
biologist-led training years and for new staff, as needed; (3) conducting terrestrial
noxious weed and aquatic nuisance vegetation monitoring annually, beginning in 2026;
(4) filing, for Commission approval, a revised ANVMP developed by a qualified
biologist that satisfies the requirements of Article 405, as outlined in the Schedule A
attachment of the February 3, 2026 Commission letter, including the identification and
evaluation of potential control methods, by February 28, 2027;10 (5) filing, for
Commission approval, a revised Shoreline Management Plan (SMP), pursuant to
Ordering paragraph (B) the 2016 Order Modifying and Approving Revised Shoreline
Management Plan (2016 SMP Order),11 which includes the details of any approval
process that allows landowners to implement specific control methods that would control
or eradicate aquatic nuisance vegetation, including documentation of agency
consultation, by September 8, 2026;12,13 (6) holding quarterly meetings with the required
practices for prevention and spread minimization, and information on eradication
methods and current Tri-Dam permitting requirements in the “How-To” Guidance Sheet.
10 Commission staff clarifies that Schedule A.9. of the February 3, 2026
Commission letter requires that the revised ANVMP include provisions to file an
ANVMP report (i.e.: an annual report) and outlines the reporting requirements in
detail. All ANVMP reports must include the information and documentation specified in
Schedule A.9.
11 South San Joaquin and Oakdale Irrigation Districts, 156 FERC ¶ 62,181
(2016).
12 In pertinent part, Article 411 of the project license required Tri-Dam to revise its
SMP and include provisions for future updates to the plan. Ordering paragraph (B) to the
2016 SMP Order requires you to file 10-year adequacy assessments and updates to the
revised SMP, if necessary. Your extension of time request, filed on August 13, 2026, is
being processed under a separate proceeding.
13 In pertinent part, Article 413 of the project license allows you to establish a
program for issuing permits for specific uses and occupancies of project lands and waters,
which may be subject to the payment of a reasonable fee to cover the costs of
administering the permit program. The allowed activities relate to physical alterations or

Project No. 2067-062 - 6 -
resource agencies to: (a) share monitoring results and mapping, (b) discuss planned and
ongoing control efforts, (c) coordinate actions on agency-managed lands within the
project boundary, (d) refine survey methods, coordinate permitting, and (e) integrate
control efforts with other habitat and resource management plans beginning on June 30,
2026; (7) implementing a comprehensive public outreach and education program to
inform shoreline property owners and visitors about terrestrial noxious weeds and aquatic
nuisance vegetation and appropriate prevention and control practices which includes the
measures outlined above as well as engaging in direct contact with individual shoreline
property owners, as appropriate and necessary and promoting awareness during
community events [unspecified]; (8) filing quarterly Process Plan progress reports with
the Commission, including documentation of agency consultation, beginning August 1,
2026; and (9) filing, for Commission approval, reports on both the terrestrial noxious
vegetation and aquatic nuisance vegetation management and control activities
implemented in 2026, including documentation of agency consultation, by December 31,
2026. Your June 3, 2026 filing included documentation of consultation with the required
resource agencies, copies of agency comments, and your responses to those comments.14
Complaints and Allegations of Non-Compliance
On April 13, 2026, Commission staff received a letter which stated that your April
3, 2026 filing was insufficient as it did not contain the missing VMP reports, focused on
future planning to comply with the requirements of Article 405 pursuant to the 2008 and
2016 Orders rather than meeting deadlines established by the Commission, and that the
current control strategy is inadequate. The letter reiterated the conclusions of the
February 3, 2026 Commission letter and requested that Commission staff shorten the
established deadline for your response. The letter also requested that Commission staff
conduct a site inspection to assess deteriorating reservoir conditions by July 31, 2026.15
On May 18, 2026, Commission staff received a letter which stated that you
refused to engage with stakeholders or provide transparency in board meetings, alleged
worsening conditions caused by unchecked aquatic vegetation as evidenced by rescue
training held at the project by Copperopolis Fire Protection District, and expressed
structures on project lands and waters – not environmental management activities;
aquatic vegetation management is not explicitly enumerated on the list.
14 Commission staff notes that you state that you have initiated consultation with
California DBW. You did not provide documentation of this consultation, however
consultation with California DBW is not required by Article 405.
15 On April 16, 2026, Commission staff issued a letter notifying you of the planned
Environmental Inspection of the project on May 19, 2026. The results of the May 19,
2026 inspection were addressed separately.

Project No. 2067-062 - 7 -
concern that there was no record that you had initiated consultation with the required
resource agencies. The letter also stated that due to your inaction, homeowners were
forced to self-fund aquatic nuisance vegetation removal on April 18 and May 10, 2026,
and again requested that Commission staff conduct a site inspection to assess
deteriorating reservoir conditions by July 31, 2026.16 The letter reiterated the
conclusions of the February 3, 2026 Commission letter and requested that Commission
staff shorten the established deadline for your response.
On June 9, 2026, Commission staff received a letter which asserted that your April
3, 2026 filing and June 3, 2026 Process Plan do not remedy Article 405 violations
identified in FERC’s February 3, 2026 Notice of Violation. The comments stated that the
Process Plan delays implementation of aquatic nuisance vegetation control measures until
2027, relies on outdated 2006 terrestrial noxious weed data, shifts the burden for
controlling aquatic nuisance vegetation onto homeowners, and published nonfunctional
application pathways for key control methods such as DASH and mechanical harvesting.
Commenters request that FERC require immediate 2026 season aquatic vegetation
control, including a valid baseline survey by July 6, 2026.17 Commenters also expressed
concern regarding potential changes to the approved aquatic nuisance vegetation control
methods. The letter also addresses the draft Shoreline Management Plan, which has yet
to be filed with the Commission, including your proposal to make private landowners
responsible for aquatic nuisance vegetation control within the project boundary.
Discussion
The description of your past terrestrial vegetation-management related activities in
your April 3, 2026 filing was vague, lacked documentation, and did not address the
remaining requirements of Article 405, pursuant to the 2008 and 2016 Orders.18 Based
16 Commission staff notes that property owners removed aquatic nuisance
vegetation in advance of Commission staff’s May 19, 2026 Environmental Inspection.
17 In our February 3, 2026 letter, Commission staff found that aquatic nuisance
vegetation has spread and establishing current conditions as the baseline for future 5-year
monitoring would be accepting degraded conditions. Commission staff also
recommended performing aquatic nuisance vegetation monitoring and control measures
annually, rather than performing a baseline survey followed by extended monitoring
periods.
18 For example: provisions for training for project staff; provisions for conducting
fire fuel inventories; provisions for the control of sudden oak death; provisions for the
mapping, monitoring, and management of wetlands and important wildlife habitat;
provisions for the protection of elderberry shrubs; provisions for the use of certified

Project No. 2067-062 - 8 -
on the lack of information, Commission staff concludes that you failed to implement the
approved terrestrial noxious vegetation monitoring and control measures within the
project boundary. Commission staff acknowledges your efforts to remedy the situation
by utilizing outside specialists and conducting a terrestrial noxious weed monitoring
survey during the 2026 growing season. However, your filings did not provide
documentation that you performed any terrestrial noxious weed control measures during
the 2026 growing season.
The Process Plan provides a plan and schedule to file a revised ANVMP for
Commission approval by February 28, 2027. You also state that you will conduct an
aquatic nuisance vegetation monitoring survey during the 2026 growing season but did
not provide a survey schedule. Commission staff acknowledges that you are in
consultation with the required resource agencies to identify and evaluate potential aquatic
nuisance vegetation control methods, and that you may propose changes to those methods
in the revised plan. However, you have not provided evidence of controlling aquatic
nuisance vegetation within the project boundary (DASH, hand pulling, mechanical
removal, and the installation of bottom barrier mats), and you did not provide a schedule
for implementation of future controls. The approved ANVMP remains in effect until any
revisions are approved by the Commission. Therefore, Commission staff reminds you
that you are required to control or eradicate terrestrial and aquatic noxious weeds
within or adjacent to the project boundary. Your jurisdiction and responsibilities
under the license apply to all lands within the project boundary, including federal-, state-,
and Tri-Dam-owned lands, as well as privately-owned lands below the 515-foot contour
elevation.
Pertaining to your responsibilities for outreach, you did not provide documentation
of the outreach efforts described in the Project Plan. Although you state that the Tri-Dam
Vegetation Management page provides access to current vegetation management
resources and permitting information, Commission staff found that the Noxious Weeds of
Tulloch Reservoir pamphlet and Tulloch Noxious Weeds Map published on the Tri-Dam
Vegetation Management webpage were created in 2006.19,20 Additionally, the Noxious
weed-free straw, rice straw, and native plant species.

75769941b1b33507ec7283b9524c342629b23b0499878d771a339c4d0eb5d5f3.
Accessed July 22, 2026.

2e8fb69e6624df9ce94edc3e86039da05eed1bbfc0069aad617ffc1dfbb3aeff. Accessed
July 22, 2026.

Project No. 2067-062 - 9 -
Weeds of Tulloch Reservoir pamphlet does not include any information about sudden oak
death, as required by paragraph (C) of the 2008 Order.21,22
You did not provide the details of any approval process that allows landowners to
implement specific control methods that would control or eradicate aquatic nuisance
vegetation pursuant to the February 3, 2026 Commission letter. Instead, you propose to
provide this information in the updated SMP. Pursuant to the requirements of Article
405, you are required to provide homeowners, dock owners, or Home Owners
Associations (HOAs) with approved methods for managing the identified aquatic
nuisance plants in the coves, shallow areas, and around boat docks of developed portions
of the shoreline in the ANVMP. Commission staff reminds you that you must provide
the details of any approval process, including federal-, state-, or local-agency
requirements, that allows landowners to implement specific control methods that would
control or eradicate aquatic nuisance vegetation in the revised ANVMP.
As part of researching the complaints, Commission staff reviewed Tri-Dam’s
website for aquatic vegetation management information and finds that the permitting
page does not include a “quick-form” application as required by the approved ANVMP.23
Commission staff reminds Tri-Dam that the current ANVMP specifically calls out
approved vegetation management methods the public can conduct on their own and
encourage you to remedy all areas of inconsistency between the ANVMP and website.
The comments received allege a lack of transparency by Tri-Dam including
concerns about limited communication with private landowners and HOAs, the use and
publication of outdated outreach materials, and failure to implement the approved
ANVMP and VMP monitoring and control methods during the 2026 season.
Additionally, the comments received requested that Commission staff reissue the
21 Paragraph (C) of the 2008 Order required you to update the noxious weed
information pamphlet to provide information about sudden oak death, including, at a
minimum: (1) information about Phytophthora ramorum pathogen that causes the
disease; (2) where the last occurrence of sudden oak death took place; and (3) suggestions
for what the public/adjacent landowners can do to prevent the spread of sudden oak
death, including avoiding unhealthy nursery plants before the distribution of the
pamphlet in 2009. Commission staff notes that this is the only provision for the control
of sudden oak death in the VMP.

6e85d31ed4719bb8434085cb8da7c7a0. Accessed July 22, 2026.
23 https://www.tridamproject.com/tulloch-reservoir-permitting-process. Accessed
July 22, 2026.

Project No. 2067-062 - 10 -
February 3, 2026 Commission letter and shorten the timeframe for response.24 The 60-
day and 120-day response deadlines were established to ensure adequate time to compile
the requested information and to develop a plan and schedule to comply with the
requirements of Article 405 in consultation with the required resource agencies.
Accordingly, the Commission did not reissue the notice of violation or adjust the
response deadline. However, Commission staff understands stakeholders’ concerns
regarding the need for consultation in the implementation of the requirements of Article
405. Commission staff finds that you must consult with the representatives of HOAs and
private landowners of land that abuts Tulloch reservoir, and any other appropriate
entities, in the development of the revised ANVMP, including any future updates or
revisions to the ANVMP and VMP. Commission staff agrees that the publication of
outreach materials that are 20 years out-of-date is insufficient to satisfy the requirements
of Article 405 and finds that you must review and update any public outreach materials to
include current information, as proposed in the Process Plan.25 You must also include
provisions for the periodic review and update of any public outreach materials in the
ANVMP and VMP.
Commission staff reiterates that all aquatic nuisance vegetation management and
control measures must be outlined in the revised ANVMP. Commission staff also
emphasizes that all resource management plans must comply with the project license, and
reminds you that the existing approved VMP, ANVMP, and SMP remain in place until
any revised plans are approved by the Commission.
In both your April 3, 2026 filing and the Process Plan, you indicate that you intend
to integrate the aquatic nuisance vegetation monitoring and control requirements into a
broader Article 405 framework for terrestrial and aquatic vegetation, habitat, and public
outreach. You address terrestrial noxious weed and aquatic nuisance vegetation
24 The April 13, May 18, and June 9, 2026 letters also requested that the
Commission impose additional requirements, including, but not limited to requiring you
to: (1) retract any and all cease-and-desist notices directed at property owners or HOAs
for use of plan-approved control methods, and promise that no such threats will be made
in the future without notifying the Commission; (2) respond to written inquiries
submitted to the Tri-Dam Joint Board; (3) maintain audio or video recordings of all Joint
Board meetings at which Article 405 compliance is discussed, and to produce these
recordings upon request; and (4) respond to the concerns of the Copperopolis Fire
Protection District. The Commission is unable to enforce requirements that fall outside
the scope of its regulatory authority and jurisdiction.
25 Commission staff acknowledges that any maps or information related the
location of known terrestrial noxious weed and aquatic nuisance vegetation problem
areas cannot be updated until you have successfully completed at least one corresponding
monitoring survey.

Project No. 2067-062 - 11 -
monitoring both together and separately throughout the Process Plan. Commission staff
notes that despite having similar elements (e.g. monitoring and control, public outreach
and education, and staff training), the VMP and ANVMP are separate resource plans, and
recommends maintaining this separation. Despite your intention to develop a new
terrestrial noxious weed monitoring survey, control plan, and schedule, you do not
propose filing a revised VMP.
For these reasons, Commission staff requires that you file a plan and schedule to
satisfy the requirements of license Article 405, pursuant to the 2008 and 2016 orders, as
outlined in the attached Schedule A in consultation with the required resource agencies.
You would then need to file any proposed amendments with the Commission for review
and approval after providing sufficient time for stakeholder consultation. Commission
staff recommends a number of steps to return into compliance with Article 405 and the
Ordered plans (Action Items and Next Steps, below).
Conclusions
Commission staff finds that you have timely filed a plan and schedule to file an
updated ANVMP, to comply with the aquatic nuisance vegetation monitoring and control
requirements of license Article 405, pursuant to the 2008 and 2016 Orders, as outlined
the February 3, 2026 Commission letter. However, upon review of the available
information, Commission staff finds that you remain in violation of Article 405 of the
project license on the basis that: (1) you did not complete the terrestrial noxious weed
monitoring and terrestrial noxious weed control requirements, beginning in 2010,
pursuant to the 2008 Order; (2) you failed to implement the approved measure for the
control of sudden oak death within the project area, as specified by the 2008 Order; (3)
you did not provide a plan and schedule to implement the approved aquatic nuisance
vegetation control methods within the project area, as required by the February 3, 2026
Commission letter; (4) you did not include documentation of your public outreach efforts,
as required by the February 3, 2026 Commission letter; and (5) you did not include the
details of any approval process that allows landowners to implement specific methods
that would control or eradicate aquatic nuisance vegetation pursuant to the February 3,
2026 Commission letter. You will remain in violation of Article 405 until you complete
the requirements as outlined above. These ongoing violations will be made a part of the
compliance history for the Project and taken into consideration regarding any future
similar events, and to determine future Commission action.
Commission staff acknowledges your efforts to develop a new plan to monitor and
control aquatic nuisance vegetation. However, Commission staff also notes that your
primary responsibility, as the licensee, is to properly implement the terms of the project
license.

Project No. 2067-062 - 12 -
Action Items and Next Steps
The timelines discussed below are intended to ensure progress towards meeting
the requirements of Article 405 of the project license and Commission approved plans.
Please take note of the following steps, which will assist you in restoring compliance
with Article 405. These items can be pursued in parallel with any effort to prepare
potential application to amend the license or plans.
1) Within 90 days of receipt of this letter, you must: (1) consult with the required
resource agencies to identify any corresponding permits necessary for private
landowners to implement each of the approved aquatic nuisance vegetation
methods on their property; (2) update the Tri-Dam Vegetation Management
webpage to reflect the information outlined above, including links to the
corresponding resource agency webpages; (3) file with the Commission
documentation of agency consultation and proof that you have corrected all Tri-
Dam vegetation management permitting information, fee schedules, outreach
materials, and the Tri-Dam Vegetation Management webpage.
2) Within 90 days of receipt of this letter, you must: (1) review and update any
public outreach materials to include current information as proposed in the Process
Plan, including a plan and schedule to update the terrestrial noxious weed and
aquatic nuisance vegetation location information and/or maps following the
successful completion of at least one of the corresponding surveys, in consultation
with the required resource agencies, allowing a minimum of 30 days for agency
review and comment; (2) file with the Commission proof that you have updated
any terrestrial noxious weed and aquatic nuisance vegetation management
outreach materials, including documentation of agency consultation, any
comments, and your responses to comments.
3) File the April-June quarterly progress report, including documentation of
consultation, comments received, and your responses to those comments, allowing
30 days for the specified entities to review and comment, including documentation
of consultation, copies of comments, and your responses to those comments before
October 31, 2026. The July-September quarterly progress report is due November
30, 2026.
4) File a plan and schedule to implement the terrestrial vegetation management
requirements of Article 405 of the project license within 120 days of receipt of
this letter for Commission approval. The attached Schedule A outlines the
requirements of Article 405 and the 2008 and 2016 Orders. The plan and schedule
shall be developed in consultation with the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, U.S.
Bureau of Land Management, California Department of Fish and Game, Calaveras
County, and Tuolumne County, the representatives of HOAs and private

Project No. 2067-062 - 13 -
landowners of land that abuts Tulloch reservoir, and any other appropriate entities,
including documentation of consultation with the specified entities, copies of
comments, and recommendations made in connection with the plan, and a
description of how the plan accommodates the comments and recommendations.
Allow a minimum of 30 days for the consulted entities to comment and to make
recommendations before filing the plan with the Commission. If you do not adopt
a recommendation, the filing shall include your reasons, based on project-specific
information.
5) File the 2026 Vegetation Management Plan report (2026 VMP report), allowing a
minimum of 30 days for review and comment, with the Commission by December
31, 2026, including documentation of the required consultations and comments,
and your responses to those comments. The attached Schedule A outlines the
terrestrial noxious weed monitoring and control requirements of Article 405 and
the 2008 and 2016 Orders. The 2026 VMP report must address the reporting
requirements outlined in the attached Schedule A.9., including documentation of
any trainings, monitoring and control measures implemented, public outreach
efforts and events, and required consultations.
6) File the 2026 Aquatic Nuisance Vegetation Management Plan report (2026
ANVMP report), allowing a minimum of 30 days for review and comment, with
the Commission by December 31, 2026, including documentation of the required
consultations and comments, and your responses to those comments. The 2026
ANVMP report must address the reporting requirements outlined in Schedule A.9.
of the February 3, 2026 Commission letter, including documentation of any
trainings, monitoring and control measures implemented, public outreach efforts
and events, and required consultations.
7) File the revised Aquatic Nuisance Vegetation Management Plan with the
Commission by February 28, 2027. The ANVMP shall satisfy the requirements of
license Article 405, pursuant to the 2008 and 2016 Orders, as outlined in the
February 3, 2026 Commission letter. Additionally, you must include provisions
for the periodic review and update of any public outreach materials in consultation
with the required resource agencies. The plan shall be developed in consultation
with the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, U.S. Bureau of Land Management,
California Department of Fish and Game, Calaveras County, and Tuolumne
County, the representatives of HOAs and private landowners of land that abuts
Tulloch reservoir, and any other appropriate entities, including documentation of
consultation with the specified entities, copies of comments, and recommendations
